title: Next Sort State
prompt: A React table header cycles through sort states when clicked. Write a helper that returns "asc" after "none", "desc" after "asc", and "none" after "desc".

explanation.beginner:
Example: nextSortState("none") produces "asc". State the comparison rule and tie behavior explicitly, and copy input before any in-place sort when the contract preserves it.

Compare “ascending becomes descending”: input ["asc"] produces "desc". Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
State the comparison rule and tie behavior explicitly, and copy input before any in-place sort when the contract preserves it.

Tempting mistake: A boolean comparator is not a valid three-way numeric comparator. Equal keys also need a predictable tie policy.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “ascending becomes descending”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
